import pandas as pd

# Load intermediate results from the given paths
intermediate_step1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_32/intermediate_step1.csv"
intermediate_step2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_32/intermediate_step2.csv"

# Read intermediate_step1.csv (has columns: ['Unnamed: 0', 'County', 'r1401', 'r1402', 'r1403_x', 'r1403_y'])
df1 = pd.read_csv(intermediate_step1_path)

# Read intermediate_step2.csv (has columns: ['County', 'r1403_x', 'r1403_y'])
df2 = pd.read_csv(intermediate_step2_path)

# The final target schema is:
# ['County': string, 'r1401': string, 'r1402': string, 'r1403_x': string, 'r1403_y': string]

# From intermediate_step1, we have 'County', 'r1401', 'r1402', 'r1403_x', 'r1403_y' plus 'Unnamed: 0'
# From intermediate_step2, we have 'County', 'r1403_x', 'r1403_y'

# The target examples show that r1403_x and r1403_y should come from the join of Source0 and Source4 (intermediate_step2),
# while r1401 and r1402 come from intermediate_step1.

# To produce the final table, we join intermediate_step1 and intermediate_step2 on 'County' to get the correct r1403_x and r1403_y,
# replacing the r1403_x and r1403_y columns from intermediate_step1 with those from intermediate_step2.

# Drop 'Unnamed: 0' from df1 as it is an index column from intermediate step
df1 = df1.drop(columns=['Unnamed: 0'])

# Merge df1 and df2 on 'County' to get r1403_x and r1403_y from df2
# We will drop r1403_x and r1403_y from df1 before merging to avoid suffixes
df1_drop_r1403 = df1.drop(columns=['r1403_x', 'r1403_y'])

# Merge on 'County'
final_df = pd.merge(df1_drop_r1403, df2, on='County', how='left')

# Reorder columns to match target schema
final_df = final_df[['County', 'r1401', 'r1402', 'r1403_x', 'r1403_y']]

# Save the final dataframe to the specified path
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read sources with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source4_32_3 and Source4_32_2 on County
join_32_3_32_2 = pd.merge(source3, source2, on="County", how="inner")

# Join Source4_32_0 and Source4_32_4 on County
join_32_0_32_4 = pd.merge(source0, source4, on="County", how="inner")

# Join the two joined tables on County
join_all_r = pd.merge(join_32_3_32_2, join_32_0_32_4, on="County", how="inner")

# Join with Source4_32_1 on County to ensure all counties are included
final_join = pd.merge(join_all_r, source1, on="County", how="inner")

# Group by County to ensure unique rows as per target keys
final = final_join.groupby("County", as_index=False).first()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
# The join created columns: County, r1401, r1402, r1403_x, r1403_y
# Because source0 and source4 both have r1403, after join they become r1403_x and r1403_y automatically
# source3 has r1401, source2 has r1402

# Select and reorder columns exactly as target schema
final = final[["County", "r1401", "r1402", "r1403_x", "r1403_y"]]

# Write output
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_32/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
